idiom_name: continuity + ordered whole-object version history + as-of lookup
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: two roles. The continuity holds the stable identity (plus any data that is truly immutable for the object's whole life) and owns an ordered history of immutable whole-object versions, each carrying the date from which it is in force. Reads are current = default as-of (now) -> newest version, and historic = as_of(date) -> the version with the greatest effective date <= date. Writes copy the version in force, apply the change to the copy and insert it at its effective date, so retroactive and scheduled amendments are ordinary inserts rather than edits of published state. Keep ordering, boundary semantics and the special cases for dates before the first version and after the last one inside one as-of operation; when the model is persisted, the continuity may be only an identity column and the versions a table keyed by (identity, effective_date).
code_sketch:
continuity: identity + history (ordered by effective)
  current()                -> version            # = as_of(today)
  as_of(date)              -> version | Missing | Invalid
  amend(effective, change) -> history.insert(copy(current()) + change, key=effective)
version: immutable snapshot { effective, ...changeable state }
pitfalls: Editing a published version instead of inserting a copy turns the history into a record of what the code did, not of what was in force.
Leaving the effective date on the current row only (or overwriting it on amendment) makes the history unnavigable and as-of reads guesswork.
Resolving reference-valued fields to 'the current' object mixes times: the version's references must either be versioned too or documented as snapshot-by-reference.

Wrong move: UPDATE the live row and log the diff in a separate table -> the object itself can no longer answer 'as of' and readers must reassemble states from log fragments that were never published -> instead copy-on-write a whole new version at its effective date.

Wrong move: version each column independently to avoid snapshot duplication -> as-of reads recombine field values that were never simultaneously true -> instead version the whole object and treat delta compression as a storage concern only.

Wrong move: resolve a version's reference-valued fields to 'the current object' -> a 2019 as-of read silently returns 2024 data for the referenced entity -> instead resolve references as-of the same date or document snapshot-by-reference as intentional.
